On the inherited no-active-catalog-query failure path, the new Databricks override suppresses DBCException and returns normally while both the JDBC connection and activeCatalogName retain their previo
GenericExecutionContext explicitly throws DBCException when catalog selection is not API-based and no active-catalog query is configured. That throw occurs before the catalog-changing query and before selectedEntityName is updated, so this path leaves the prior catalog selected. The new Databricks override calls the inherited method inside a try block, catches DBCException without rethrowing it, and only assigns activeCatalogName after a successful inherited call. Thus the failure becomes normal completion with the old catalog still active. DBExecUtils.changeDefaultObject directly invokes setDefaultCatalog from a method declared to throw DBException, showing a caller path where propagation would abort the operation; the changed derived-context initialization also invokes it directly. E20 establishes that the change makes Databricks use this dedicated context.
Impact: Caused by the change: The change introduces and installs a Databricks-specific override that intercepts DBCException from the existing generic implementation. On the explicit pre-switch failure path, the inherited method performs no catalog switch and never reaches its state update; the override also skips activeCatalogName assignment but swallows the exception. Consequently callers receive normal completion instead of the failure that previously propagated and could abort their operation.
